statement: The core summary is accurate, but the benchmark description in the Spanish follow-up needs correction. Section 4.4 and Table 2 use fifty 500-character Wikipedia extracts across five languages, with substitution followed by intra-word anagramming. They report 93.8% token recovery for the combined two-stage pipeline. They did not inject 2% transcription noise. That level is a new test setting for the swarm. Section 5.3's 0.996 and 2.454 are fitted average inversion counts under separate glyph or letter orders, equivalent to minimum adjacent swaps to reach those orders. Section 6 proposes extending the anagram model to reorder whole words within lines, and suggests softened emissions for noise generally. The Spanish and English reversal checks are narrower swarm variants. Primary source: https://aclanthology.org/Q16-1006.pdf
